Acute mesenteric ischemia (especially early or non-occlusive) fits the sudden severe pain and hematochezia, though absence of vomiting and systemic signs makes it slightly less likely than ischemic colitis (which is more common and often less catastrophic initially). IBD flare is less likely without prior diagnosis, chronic symptoms, or systemic features (e.g., weight loss, nocturnal diarrhea), but de novo presentation can occur—hence included as a lower-probability consideration.
